messages:
Sam: Heads-up — gateway collector started OOMing under heavy trace export load this morning, heap climbs until container restart.
Maya: ah we saw a spike too, different cluster. any obvious exporter backpressure?
Sam: exporters were healthy; batch processor shoves everything into memory while endpoint latency spikes.
Ralph: Are we using the default batch processor settings? timeout/max_queue_size?
Sam: default. I attached the relevant snippet from the pipeline config:
```yaml
service:
  pipelines:
    traces:
      receivers: [otlp]
      processors: [batch]
      exporters: [otlp/ingest, logging]
processors:
  batch:
    timeout: 200ms
    send_batch_size: 512
```
Maya: 512 is pretty aggressive for time-to-first-byte when ingest has 100–300ms p99. queues balloon.
Ingrid: Could we set max_queue_size or switch to per-signal bounded queues? we already have per-tenant rules for metrics.
Ralph: Per-signal pipeline would help — keep traces separate from metrics/census. but that means more memory overhead overall unless we cap each queue.
Terry: +1 on bounded queues. Also consider a small local persistent buffer (WAL) so we don't just drop spans when memory is full.
Sam: WAL solves durability but increases IO and complexity for sidecar. For gateway maybe we prefer shedding vs backpressure to callers.
Maya: What do we want upstream to see? 429s from gateway or dropped spans silently? Ops would prefer explicit errors.
DevX: For SDK users, a 429 is actionable. Silent drop messes with customer SLAs. we should prefer backpressure signals.
Ralph: Implement backpressure by returning gRPC ResourceExhausted? but OTLP exporters often have retries — could amplify load. need retry-aware strategy.
Ingrid: Maybe gateway returns 429 with Retry-After; sidecars do local buffering + shed oldest spans if disk pressure.
Sam: Another angle: switch batch processor to dynamic sizing based on endpoint latency histogram. Have the processor reduce send_batch_size when endpoint p99 > X.
Maya: Would need metrics into runtime to inform that control loop. doable. but adds tuning surface.
Terry: Also think about retention and TTL at the gateway — keep recent spans short TTL (1h) in mem cache for dedupe/kv cache and older are offloaded to WAL/dropped if under pressure.
Sam: Could we limit max total queued spans per tenant across all pipelines (global cap) and then route overflow to dedicated draining pool?
Ralph: That matches our routing policy idea: normal traffic -> gateway fast path, overflow -> dedicated overflow pool (lower priority exporters).
Ingrid: UX question: Console should expose per-tenant queue usage, queue caps, and how many spans were shed vs retried. otherwise customers will be confused.
DevX: +1. Small widget on route detail: current queued, p99 export latency, recent 429 rate.
ops-bot: Incident summary: gateway OOM on prod-a causing ~3min ingestion blip. Restarted automatically.
deploy-bot: canary gateway image v1.42 deployed to prod-a at 08:12 UTC (no rollback).
Maya: For immediate mitigation I'm going to reduce send_batch_size to 128 and add max_queue_size: 10000 on the batch processor in prod-a.
Sam: sounds good. can you also enable exporter circuit breaker (fail fast) for ingest to avoid retry amplification?
Maya: yes will add circuit breaker config and a 10s exporter timeout.
Terry: Longer term we should prototype:
- per-signal bounded queues with configurable caps
- local WAL for sidecars only
- gateway overflow routing to dedicated low-priority exporters
- console metrics for queued spans / shed counts / 429s
Ralph: I'll draft a proposal doc for the control loop approach + API for queue caps and circuit breakers.
Ingrid: Thanks — please include failure modes (disk full for WAL, retry storms) and migration steps.
Sam: Great. @Maya can you open a quick PR with the prod-a change and a rollback plan?
Maya: On it, PR incoming in ~20m. :thumbsup:
Sam: Thanks everyone.
